peers.scope: Managed C/H owners, transfer/resize/cache integration, native lease API; controls 1–12 and 19–23; eight-line build registration
Native Windows/Linux allocator/accounting/permissions and platform guard; controls 13–18, final 14/16 assertion delta and WrapperProbe/24
Complete production and full 24-control predecessor; exact external-SAB, partial-table and final 14/16 assertion deltas.

limits: No build, actual metadata query, runtime or full HTTP/FileHandle claim.
Managed storage hooks activate only on Windows and Linux; other platforms preserve their prior routes.
Existing QuickJS 2 GiB maximum is retained; bytecode layout/version is unchanged.
Lease is a native allocation entitlement and intrinsic snapshot span, not a JS root or a promise that RAB-shrunk pages remain writable.
Detach/resize remain enabled; no staged copyback or blanket RAB/GSAB restriction.
Public foreign ArrayBuffer/SAB storage keeps its original callback and returns lease status 0 with empty output.
Managed runtimes reject foreign SAB serialization with an ordinary TypeError before table admission; same-process SAB reader pointer tables remain trusted input.
No claim that the original Node FSReq explicitly retained a V8 BackingStore.
Broader unchanged typed-array/DataView semantics and cross-platform libuv/FileHandle scheduling remain independently qualified.
